steps.title: Why Duplicates Occur
steps.text: Message duplicates arise from producer retries, consumer crashes before offset commit, consumer group rebalances, network partitions, and transaction rollbacks.

steps.title: Delivery Semantics
steps.text: At-most-once risks data loss. At-least-once (the default) may produce duplicates. Exactly-once uses transactional processing for zero loss and zero duplicates.

steps.title: Deduplication Pipeline
steps.text: Layer deduplication with Bloom filters for fast pre-filtering, LRU caches for accurate bounded-memory checks, and optional database lookups for confirmed duplicates.

steps.title: Idempotent Operations
steps.text: Design operations that are safe to repeat. Use database upserts instead of increments, and include idempotency keys in every message for duplicate detection.

steps.title: Strategy Comparison
steps.text: Choose from HashSet (fast, unbounded), LRU cache (bounded memory), Bloom filter (very low memory), time-based (short windows), or database-backed (durable) deduplication.
